core_problem: Existing specialized pre-trained language models (like BioBERT and BioClinicalBERT) for medical NLP are often overparameterized and resource-intensive.
methodology_summary: Development of efficient lightweight clinical transformers using Knowledge Distillation (KD) and continual learning, with parameter counts ranging from 15 million to 65 million.
datasets_eval: Several standard datasets covering clinical text-mining tasks (e.g., MedNLI mentioned in limitations context).
empirical_results: The developed compact models performed comparably to larger models (BioBERT, ClinicalBioBERT) and significantly outperformed other compact models trained on general or biomedical data. Initializing ClinicalDistilBERT with a biomedical checkpoint significantly improved performance on MedNLI.
explicit_limitations: The models are heavy in size and number of parameters, making them unsuitable for devices with limited memory and processing capacity.
